parts.text: # Ticket status ledger

Status values: `todo` → `planned` or `questions` → `ready` → `in-progress` → `review` → `done`, or `blocked` (PROCESS.md section 13). Complexity: `low`, `medium` or `high` from the plan (PROCESS.md section 4); it picks the test-author and builder models. Phase 0 ratings were set by the orchestrator on 2026-10-18 from the v1 plans (no planner rating existed); the planner re-rates a plan it re-validates.

Only the orchestrator edits this file (enforced by hook). It records each stage's result: planner → `planned`/`questions`; Stage 2 → `ready`; build → `in-progress`, `review`; reviewers' verdict → `done` (with commit) or back to `in-progress`; three failed reviews or a question for Josh → `blocked`.

A ticket starts only when every ticket in its `depends_on` (in `tickets.json`, base IDs already expanded) is `done`. The Depends on column here is the original text, for reading only. Notes also records the models used for each dispatch and why (PROCESS.md section 4). Notes holds plan deviations (what the merged code does differently from its plan; dependents' plans are re-validated against it) and `needs-josh-confirm` wording (user-visible text no plan covered, listed in the phase PR for Josh). Pick tickets with `node vault/tools/next_ticket.mjs`; validate with `--check` (done needs a commit hash, blocked needs a note, statuses must be known, STATUS.md and tickets.json must list the same tickets).

# Questions ledger: open and escalated

Three files, one ledger (Josh 2026-10-28): `QUESTIONS.md` holds open and escalated questions (new questions are added there); `QUESTIONS-answered.md` holds answered questions the build still needs; `QUESTIONS-archive.md` holds answered questions it no longer needs (every ticket named is done and no unfinished plan or phase file cites them). Rows move only whole and unchanged, by `node vault/tools/next_ticket.mjs --sort-questions` (rule in that file). Look a Q-ID up in all three files.

Chain of command: asking agent → orchestrator → specialist (calc-auditor / security-reviewer / code-reviewer) → Josh. No citation, no answer. Business and product decisions always go to Josh. Full rules: `vault/PROCESS.md`, Stage 2.

Statuses: `open`, `answered-agent`, `escalated` (waiting on Josh), `answered-josh`, `confirmed-josh` (an agent answer Josh confirmed). Agent answers not yet confirmed when Stage 3 starts stand as written.

IDs never change or get reused. Josh's answers are also appended to the decisions file for the spec area (`vault/spec/decisions/<area>.md`; index in `vault/spec/decisions/INDEX.md`). Until Oct 18, 2026 they went to `vault/spec/decisions.md`, now split into that folder.

questions.question: The phase auditor runs on Fable, which may draw usage credits on a subscription. Use Fable for phase audits, or Opus?
questions.answer: Fable uses existing usage credits with no auto-refill. Use Fable for phase audits; fall back to Opus if the credits run out.

questions.question: What does each ticket's check run: the full test suite (current setup; safest, but slow by about Phase 10 with three device sizes and several hundred browser tests), or the phase's tests plus a smoke set, with CI running everything on develop? The planning session recommended the second; changing it edits rule 3 in `tickets/README.md` and `scripts/gate.mjs`.
questions.answer: Each ticket's check runs the phase's tests plus a smoke set; the full suite runs at the phase gate. Rule 3 in `tickets/README.md` is updated; the EZD-001 plan specifies the `scripts/gate.mjs` change, which Josh applies (exact change in `vault/questions/phase-00-for-josh.md`).

questions.question: Brief: one branch per ticket with CI and a preview, squash-merge to main per ticket. Current setup: ticket branches stay local, squash to develop, Josh merges develop → main once per phase. Which?
questions.answer: Keep develop → main per phase. Merging to main per ticket would deploy production every ticket, which conflicts with the brief's own 3.5 (production only at a phase gate). Previews come from develop and the phase PR. Josh can override.

questions.question: After the export, is the vault or the claude.ai document the source of truth?
questions.answer: The vault. The claude.ai spec, tickets and mockups are frozen as of Oct 11 and superseded; two editable copies would drift.

questions.question: Who may edit spec files during the build?
questions.answer: Nobody edits the section files. Changes are recorded as Josh answers in `spec/decisions.md`, which overrides the spec text (the brief allowed the coordinator to edit spec files with a decisions row; this is stricter, so builders cannot "fix" the spec to match code). questions.question: No source sets the security parameters of the contract. Options: (a) accept the planner's values: every request EZ Draft sends (API calls and webhooks) is signed with HMAC-SHA256 over `<t>.<METHOD>.<path and query>.<body>` with the tenant's signing secret, plus an `EZDraft-Tenant` header; EZ Binder learns the tenant id from a signed `connection.check` delivery at Connect (no fourth value beyond R32's three); timestamp tolerance 300 seconds; signing secret and inbound key at least 32 random bytes; sign-on codes at least 128 bits (22 base64url characters), matching EZD-1705's share-token floor; (b) the security-reviewer sets different values or a different scheme, and T11, T12 and T13 follow it.
questions.answer: (a) with three changes: the HMAC-SHA256 signed string includes the tenant (`<t>.<EZDraft-Tenant>.<METHOD>.<path and query>.<raw body>`) and EZ Binder binds the tenant at `connection.check` only after the signature verifies and the header equals the body; signing secret and inbound key are 32 CSPRNG bytes (43 base64url chars) and Connect refuses shorter; EZ Draft issues 256-bit sign-on codes (contract floor stays 128 bits), stored hashed, single use. Tolerance 300 s accepted. Josh can override.
questions.source: 11 Security; 07 Delivery rules; R32; R15; 03 rule 11; R26 R14; phase-17 EZD-1705

questions.question: What is EZ Draft for, and what is held for v2?
questions.answer: EZ Draft makes a clean, measured plan the crew can build from, plus a permit set when needed; it helps clients decide on selections with AI photoreal renders of the exact items; any layout can be built or changed. Every feature is built for v1; nothing is held for v2.

questions.question: Who may start a project, measure and draw?
questions.answer: Any staff member, including crew-level, can start a project. Measuring and drawing are not tied to one person: anyone starts, anyone finishes, in any order; any staff member may be sent mid-job to re-measure or add measurements. Fully customizable permissions decide who can do what, changeable at any time.

questions.question: Add plumbing and mechanical drawings to v1?
questions.answer: Yes. v1 adds plumbing sheets (supply and drain locations, plumbing diagrams such as riser or isometric, plumbing calculations if the department needs them), mechanical sheets and calculations, and a tile layout sheet that needs client sign-off. Plumbing and mechanical rules and calculations are researched before Round 3 and checked there.

questions.question: Should EZ Draft check that the drawings match the scope of work?
questions.answer: Yes, for every department. Example (Boca Raton rejection): the scope listed electrical the client had removed and the drawings had no electrical. Scope and drawings must agree both ways. Rule details in Round 3.

questions.question: When is a load calculation needed, and where do the common loads come from?
questions.answer: Load calculation for a panel change, a service change or new circuits. Common loads are data: every new account gets a default set, and the user can add new ones and edit existing ones in Settings. Values in Round 3.

questions.question: Engineer, architect and structural work?
questions.answer: A seal box is always available on permit drawings. Minor structural items (for example moving a wall) can be drawn; EZ Draft builds no structural calculations.

questions.question: Disclaimer in the terms only, or on screen too?
questions.answer: On screen as well as in the terms, on basically every page, along the lines of: "This is for design and planning purposes. These calculations and codes must be confirmed by the user and a licensed person within the jurisdiction." Exact wording and placement in Round 2.

questions.question: Are security, performance, accessibility and screen states a late hardening phase?
questions.answer: No. The proper architecture comes from the start: each slice meets and tests the security, performance, accessibility and screen-state rules for what it builds. Backups, the terms page and the on-screen disclaimer move to the first slices; slices 52 and 53 keep only the final whole-app checks and code-rule verification.

questions.question: Are the newer boards the mockups for screens still labelled "not in mockup"? (prep C1-C4)
questions.answer: Yes. Boards S01b, S15b, S17c and S19-S22 are the mockups; the "not in mockup" labels come off where the board shows the control.

questions.question: New project wizard: dialog or full page, and which fields? (prep C3, C16)
questions.answer: A dialog over the Projects page, as board S01b shows. It adds a Scope of work field (R28) and a Foreman picker (R31).

questions.question: May a crew sign-in link be shown on screen? (prep C11)
questions.answer: The person sending an invite gets a link they can send to make sign-in easy for staff. The everyday sign-in email link is still never shown on screen (Q-0035).

questions.question: Lock release and share-link expiry: fixed or settings? (prep C12)
questions.answer: Settings, starting at 5 minutes and 30 days.

questions.question: Ways to start a project? (prep C13)
questions.answer: Six: Polycam scan, PDF, DXF, supplier kitchen PDF, field measure, blank.

questions.question: EZ Binder connection and change orders in v1?
questions.answer: No EZ Binder connection in v1; the connector is built later together with the EZ Binder side (BACKLOG.md). Projects and clients are entered in EZ Draft. EZ Draft offers a downloadable "Scope PDF" (written scope plus before/after drawings or renders, from any revision or design option) that Josh attaches to an estimate or change order in EZ Binder.

questions.question: Closeout?
questions.answer: A simple workflow with no blockers and nothing the system detects: a "Mark complete" action for anyone with permission; the project moves to a Completed filter on Projects, stays viewable and can be reopened.

questions.question: Must every added product go into the catalog?
questions.answer: No. When adding a product the user can choose not to add it to the catalog, since many items are one-off uses.

questions.question: Which building departments first?
questions.answer: Build and test first: unincorporated Palm Beach County, Boca Raton, West Palm Beach. Research in Round 4: North Palm Beach, Delray Beach, Boynton Beach, Lake Worth Beach, Wellington, Riviera Beach. The Broward presets (Broward County, Fort Lauderdale, Coral Springs) stay as options.

questions.question: Phase list and order? (prep C7)
questions.answer: The 53 slices are the phase list, with the moves recorded in PHASES.md (Round 1 approval). Work is broken down within each phase; tickets and specs carry enough that an agent need not read other files, and stay short. 3D and renders are built in order with no wait for a real job; the build runs 24/7.

questions.question: May gaps the stories did not touch wait for their round?
questions.answer: Yes: screens in Round 2, calculations and the plumbing and mechanical research in Round 3, outside services and departments in Round 4.

questions.question: Is pricing removed from v1 along with EZ Binder?
questions.answer: No (answer a): pricing stays in EZ Draft as the spec has it (catalog prices, render allowance, cost and sell-price permissions). Only the EZ Binder hand-off goes.

questions.question: Each company gets a storage limit, and users are regularly prompted to delete older data. What is the limit, what happens when a company reaches it, and how often are users prompted?
questions.answer: One cap for all of a company's stored data: 100 GB. Every office user is reminded at 80%, 90% and 100%. At 100% the company is blocked from storing more; files already stored can still be opened, exported and sent (R-032 Option B behaviour, limit and reminders as Josh set them). Sent files are no longer permanent (reverses R24 #4a and 11 Data retention "Sent versions ... are permanent"): a company may download them, delete them for good, or keep them on EZ Draft within its limit; this needs a ticket that removes the sent-file lock (`sent_files_soft_delete`, EZD-025) and updates the spec, numbered when the storage-limit work is planned. The Supabase spend cap is decided at launch, when the production project is created (Q-0113).

questions.question: Charging other companies for EZ Draft: which payment provider (for example Stripe), which plans and prices, and is there a free trial? Needed before phase 53 is planned, not before.
questions.answer: Stripe (Billing and Tax). $50 a month per company, 5 office users included, unlimited field and crew users, $10 a month per extra office user. Free trial: 14 days, no card, no AI renders. Renders: an included monthly allowance capped at $3 of render cost per company; unused allowance rolls over one month only; renders past the allowance are charged $1 per fast render and $5 per photoreal render; each render allows one free redo if it does not turn out well. How the allowance, rollover, redo and extra charges are tracked and shown to users is still to be designed (Josh 2026-10-28); open detail: whether the redo applies to included and extra renders alike and whether a redo counts toward the $3 cap.

questions.question: Render credits for paying companies (follows Q-0237): how render use, the $3 cost cap, rollover, redo and extra charges are tracked and shown.
questions.answer: Render credits replace dollars for paying companies (supersedes Round 24 #18 and S15f decision 2 for them): 100 credits a month per company; fast 1, standard 2, photoreal 5 credits; extra credits $1 each (so $1 fast, $2 standard, $5 photoreal); unused credits roll over one month then expire, oldest used first. The $3 cap is on real provider cost: when a company's included renders reach $3 of cost in a month before its credits run out, included renders stop and extras begin. Redo: an extra (paid) render gets one free redo with the same input and settings; a redo of an included render uses credits. Shown: the tier picker shows credits per tier and the balance; an extra render needs a confirm ("This render is extra: $N on your next bill") every time; after an extra render a Redo button (free once); Settings Render models shows credits used, carried over and left, and extras this month in dollars; office users are reminded at 80% and 100% of credits used; provider cost is shown only to the operator. Tracked in an append-only credit record (grant, rollover, use, redo, extra, expiry) linked to the render with its real cost; extras go to Stripe as metered usage keyed by render id. Trial: renders blocked with a notice. Worth Properties (tenant 1) is never limited by credits or company billing: no credit balance, no extra charges, no subscription (Josh 2026-10-28).

questions.question: `requestSignIn` hides the hook's 403 and every 429 except `over_request_rate_limit` (Q-0174 (a)). The plan does not say what any other Auth error (a 500, a network failure) does. The builder throws `sign_in_request_failed` (a 500, per docs/architecture.md Errors and logging "500 unexpected", "nothing fails silently"); since an email-send failure can only happen for a known address, that answer differs from an unknown address's. Keep the 500, or answer `{ step: 'code' }` for every error?
questions.answered_by: security-reviewer (EZD-007d, 2026-10-20); confirmed by Josh 2026-10-20 ("confirm", phase-00-for-josh.md section 2)
questions.answer: Keep the 500. Q-0174 (a) hides only answers an attacker can trigger at will (hook 403, resend 429); a 5xx or network failure is not, and a hook or database outage fails unknown addresses the same way. The one asymmetric case (a send outage for a known address) leaks nothing beyond the public Auth endpoint already escalated as Q-0175, while `{ step: 'code' }` on a failed send would leave the person with no email and no error. questions.question: EZD-153 (the release safety check must catch tables and functions created in text it cannot read) failed its extra round 3 (Q-0331 (a)), so it is blocked again. Every earlier finding is closed: both reviewers confirmed the quoted-name gap (Q-0331), the missing E10 TL3 test row and the docs range are fixed, the gate is green and Production-sensitive changes PASS. But the security-reviewer found two new ways through, and the code-reviewer one minor: (1) security: the scanner treats letters outside plain ASCII (`é`, a non-breaking space) as punctuation, while PostgreSQL reads them as part of a name, so `select 1 as é$t$ into x from (select 1) as x$t$` hides a table create from every rule; (2) security: inside a PL/pgSQL body the scanner skips the `select … into` rule, but `for r in explain analyze select … into t loop` and `return query explain analyze select … into t` create the table; (3) minor: the `checkWithoutTag` comment lists three reasons, the code has four (`string_escape`). Scanner side checked by the orchestrator this session: both spellings give no finding, the plain control gives `hidden_create`; that PostgreSQL 17.11 really creates the tables is the security-reviewer's own probe. This is the fourth round where each fix closed every named case and the reviewer found a new spelling the hand-written reader sees differently from PostgreSQL (comments, E-strings, quoted names, now non-ASCII names and EXPLAIN): the approach of listing spellings is not converging. (ii) refused attempts are not counted. (iii) a success does not clear earlier failures (the earlier "success clears the count" sentence is withdrawn; it was not in Q-0094). (iv) rolling windows. (v) IPv6 by /64, IPv4 by full address. (vi) changed: no IP counting only when VERCEL_ENV is unset (local, CI); on Vercel, loopback, private, carrier-NAT, link-local, unparseable or missing addresses count as "unknown"; read only the client-IP header Vercel guarantees to overwrite (confirm on pinned platform). questions.question: When Auth refuses a password sign-in for its captcha (no password was checked), does the attempt count toward the password throttle? Q-0104 (i) counts every wrong password and does not count Supabase 429 and 5xx, and does not name this case. Options: (a) do not count it, like 429 and 5xx (recommended by the planner: the password was never checked, and counting it would let a script without a captcha token use up a person's password attempts); (b) count it, as `signInWithPassword` counts every other refusal today.
questions.answer: (a): a captcha refusal does not count toward the password throttle (per-email or per-IP), like a Supabase 429 or 5xx: Auth checks the captcha before the credentials, so no password was checked, and counting it would let a script with no token lock a person out of password sign-in for 15 minutes. As merged, actions.ts counts it (only 429 and status 0/5xx settle), so EZD-034 adds a settle branch matched on Auth's captcha error code, never on bare HTTP 400 (a wrong password is also 400 and stays counted).

questions.question: Chromium drops the body of a non-GET response (the app's server-action POSTs, `POST /auth/confirm` and `POST /sign-in`) when the app's own navigation commits before the read returns, and Playwright never settles the read of one aborted after its headers (vault/plans/EZD-163.md C6 iii-iv; G1, P7, P8), so no read and no safe refetch can give it; the harness leak checks (T12, T21, T23) would fail every run or at random. Options: (a) count such non-GET bodies as unread (`null`) and allow them for `fetch` and `xhr` only, while every GET, document and script body must still be read or fetched again (stricter than merged T12, which read only documents and scripts, and T21/T23, which counted unread bodies as clean); (b) route every request through the test (`context.route` + `route.fetch` + `route.fulfill`) so every body is read in Node first, at the cost of buffering every response, changing how app traffic flows under test and stacking on the net-guard route; (c) check bodies of documents and scripts only, as merged T12 did. Planner's lean: (a). It narrows a secret-leak check, so it is Josh's call (rule 16).
questions.answered_by: Josh (2026-10-27: "I want B", after asking which is more secure and robust)
questions.answer: (b), limited to the three leak-check tests (T12, T21, T23): only those specs route requests through the test (`context.route` + `route.fetch` + `route.fulfill`) so every response body, form-submit and server-action replies included, is read in Node before the page gets it; every other test and the app run unrouted. Josh chose it as the more secure and robust option (CLAUDE.md rule 18): no unread body, no blind spot where secrets are most likely. EZD-163 set to todo for the planner to re-plan with this answer.
